cohort: 264,755 births from a Canadian multicentre birth cohort
finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with an increased risk of maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality, and the risk of adverse outcomes varied by mode of delivery subgroup.
mod_finding: Assisted vaginal delivery and intrapartum cesarean delivery were associated with higher risks of adverse outcomes compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery, while planned cesarean delivery reduced the risk of some outcomes but increased the risk of others.
